Every candidate also needs a rule check: - no real data in build; - a full reset in prepare; - eval that works for any batch size from 1 to 1024 within 5 s; - no TTA. The run descriptions for E024 and E025 say "On E012", but their times (6.45 s and 7.26 s) show they actually ran on the tip. But it cost +0.81 s, almost all of it per-step launch overhead (~2.3 ms per step). **Top priority (5): turn Muon into speed.** - **I032** keeps the Muon math identical but makes it cheap: same-shape filters run through one batched Newton-Schulz, and the whole Muon step goes inside the captured train-step graph. Expected time is ~6.65-6.85 s. - **I033** spends Muon's gain on fewer epochs, cutting from 11 to 9.5. Expected accuracy is ~0.755, at ~6.27 s on the current Muon code or ~5.8 s if I032's fused version works. Either would be a new best. **Other exploit ideas:** - **Batch 2048 (priority 4):** a further throughput gain of -2 to -4% expected, with some risk of losing accuracy. - **Whole-phase CUDA graphs (priority 2):** removes the host gaps between graph replays; -3 to -6% expected. **Explore ideas, each one cheap and decisive:** - **Whitening-bias training cut from 3 to 0.5 epochs (priority 3):** a schedule constant left over from 37-epoch runs; costs no time. - **Max + average pooling before the head (priority 2):** a near-free test of whether the 100-class head is limited by its feature dimension. - **Block 3 widened from 704 to 896 (priority 2):** a dose-response point for the block-3 width lever. The noise floor (H1.1.3) is handled by a rule in I033: any new tip that clears 0.753 by less than 0.3 pp is rerun and pooled before it replaces E024.
